free_tier.stated: $5 in free compute credit to start; no provider account needed. Sandboxes deduct from the credit balance at the listed per-provider compute rates, and a 5% platform fee applies when buying more credits.
free_tier.notes: A one-time $5 credit at signup, not a recurring allowance. Compute is billed from the credit balance at the published rates; with BYOK the provider bills compute directly. The $5 is not a per-hour or per-sandbox quota and no separate free sandbox count is published.

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: the offer is routed compute, and no single-object size cap is published on the pricing or docs pages
per_object_cap.notes: A sandbox has a size-specific disk ceiling in the rate table (for example 50 GB for a 1 vCPU / 2 GB sandbox on cloudflare); that is a machine size, not a per-object cap.

retention.stated: A sandbox keeps running until destroyed or its lifetime expires; sandboxes expire by default after 30 minutes. Files survive while the sandbox exists; destroying it deletes the sandbox and its files.
retention.notes: Retention is tied to the sandbox lifecycle, not a fixed byte-retention window. The docs state a 30-minute default expiry and that closing a terminal or disconnecting a preview does not destroy a sandbox.

egress.terms: No separate egress price is published for routed compute: sandboxes deduct from prepaid credit at the listed compute rates, and code running in a sandbox can reach the internet. A sandbox port can be exposed through sandbox_url, which makes it reachable from the public internet. Outbound traffic on an operator's own provider keys is billed by that provider.

interface_detail: REST API at https://platform.computesdk.com/api/v1 with an OpenAPI spec; a TypeScript SDK (npm computesdk), a CLI (npm @computesdk/cli), and an MCP server at https://platform.computesdk.com/mcp. A console at platform.computesdk.com handles sign-up, keys, provider keys and billing.
tooling: npm install computesdk for the SDK; npm install @computesdk/cli or curl -fsSL https://computesdk.com/install | sh for the compute CLI; a hosted MCP server and a REST API are also published.
chaining: Routes one sandbox API across many compute providers and bills from one credit balance, so an agent workload can be moved to a specific provider or to an own key without changing the API used by the user.

limits_note: Rates in the table are normalized to USD per hour for comparison; each row lists a billing increment when available, and most rows read 'Not specified'. A quote does not reserve capacity, and being listed in the catalog or benchmarks does not grant access to a provider account.
binding_note: The $5 one-time credit is the first constraint for a new account: at the lowest published sandbox rate of $0.03 an hour (sandbox0 small, 1 vCPU / 2 GB) it covers about 166 hours, and at the highest sandbox rate of $5.4528 an hour (vercel 3xlarge) about 0.9 hours, before the 30-minute default expiry or the 240-request-per-minute API rate becomes relevant.

identity_cost.detail: An organization is required: 'Every hosted sandbox, provider credential, API key and Actions run belongs to an organization. Start at platform.computesdk.com.' The console sign-up form shows a workspace address, a password field of 'At least 8 characters' and a Terms acceptance, and offers a sign-in link for existing accounts; browser login for the CLI opens a browser and saves a session locally. The pages read do not state whether the address must be verified, and name no phone number, ID document or institution. No card is needed to use the $5 credit; credits beyond it are bought in Settings -> Billing.

reliability_note: No SLA: the terms state 'SLA: None' and only commercially reasonable efforts to keep the service available. Sandboxes bill until destroyed or expired and a 429 rate limit applies at 240 requests per minute per connection; closing a terminal does not stop billing.
confidence_note: The publisher's own pricing, llms.txt, llms-full.txt, authentication, billing, terms pages and console sign-up text were read on 2026-11-24; the rate table in llms-full.txt states it was updated 2026-11-21. The sign-up form's visible text does not enumerate all fields, so its exact identity requirement is partial.
